records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: An operational dispatch-desk tool for reconciling mismatched references by comparing an overnight spreadsheet with the daily export. Personally built with Python and SQL, using a Python parser, SQL checks, Git, and a PostgreSQL production database. Operators used visible warnings and understandable exceptions; supervisors made final dispatch decisions.

decisions.reason: The profile summary and personal context are stated directly, and the listed denials accurately reflect the source.
The employer, role, dates, personal project work, coworker training, handbook, skills, and linked achievements are supported by the source.

The summary says operators used visible warnings and understandable exceptions, but the source says operators preferred a warning and supervisors wanted understandable exceptions. It turns preferences into implemented use and misattributes whose preference it was.
The source supports training 12 coworkers in two workshops, writing the handbook, and that workshops occurred after coworkers could use the tool; it also says exact dates are unavailable.
The source supports the six-run reconciliation-time reduction as a team result, the personal contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and the correction that delivery speed was not measured.
The source supports using Python to build Dispatch Loom and personally writing its Python parser.
The source supports using SQL to build Dispatch Loom and personally writing its SQL checks.
The source explicitly identifies PostgreSQL as the production database.
The source explicitly identifies Git as the version-control tool.
The source supports personally training dispatch coworkers in workshops and writing the plain-language handbook.
The degree, institution, and dates are stated directly in the source.
The source supports the certificate name and date, and clarifies that it was course completion rather than a professional license.
